title.en: Phrasal Verbs (give up, put off, come up with, look forward to)
title.es: Los phrasal verbs (give up, put off, come up with, look forward to)

text.en: A phrasal verb is a verb plus an adverb or preposition whose meaning is not the sum of the words: give up = stop trying, put off = postpone. Spanish has a one-word verb (rendirse, posponer), but everyday English prefers the phrasal verb. Three important questions: is it separable (“turn it off”), does it take an object, and does it have three words (“run out of”).
text.es: Un phrasal verb es un verbo más un adverbio o preposición cuyo significado no es la suma de las palabras: give up = rendirse, put off = posponer. El español tiene un verbo de una palabra (rendirse, posponer), pero el inglés cotidiano prefiere el phrasal verb. Tres preguntas importantes: ¿se puede separar («turn it off»)?, ¿lleva objeto? y ¿tiene tres palabras («run out of»)?

text.en: A noun object can go between the two parts or after them: turn off the light, turn the light off. A pronoun always goes between the two parts: turn it off, not “turn off it”.
text.es: El objeto nominal puede ir entre las dos partes o después: turn off the light, turn the light off. El pronombre siempre va entre las dos partes: turn it off, no «turn off it».

examples.es: Please turn off the light. Please turn it off.

tr.en: Please turn off the light. Please turn it off.
tr.es: Por favor, apaga la luz. Apágala.

examples.es: They put off the meeting. They put it off.

tr.en: They put off the meeting. They put it off.

text.en: The object always follows the whole verb: look after the kids, look after them. Others like this are get over, run into, look into.
text.es: El objeto siempre va después de todo el verbo: look after the kids, look after them. Otros así son get over, run into, look into.

examples.es: She looks after her little brother.

tr.en: She looks after her little brother.

examples.es: He finally got over his cold.

tr.en: He finally got over his cold.
tr.es: Por fin se recuperó de su resfriado.

text.en: Verb + adverb + preposition, inseparable: run out of, put up with, come up with, get along with, look forward to. After look forward to comes the -ing form, because to is a preposition.
text.es: Verbo + adverbio + preposición, no separable: run out of, put up with, come up with, get along with, look forward to. Después de look forward to va la forma -ing, porque to es una preposición.

examples.es: We have run out of milk.

tr.en: We have run out of milk.

examples.es: I'm looking forward to seeing you.

tr.en: I'm looking forward to seeing you.

text.en: The particle often changes the meaning: give up (stop trying), put off (postpone), call off (cancel), turn down (refuse), carry on (continue), break down (stop working).
text.es: La partícula suele cambiar el significado: give up (rendirse), put off (posponer), call off (cancelar), turn down (rechazar), carry on (continuar), break down (descomponerse).

examples.es: He turned down the job offer.

tr.en: He turned down the job offer.

examples.es: My car broke down on the way to work.

tr.en: My car broke down on the way to work.
tr.es: Mi carro se descompuso camino al trabajo.

text.en: A pronoun cannot follow the adverb: not “turn off it”, but “turn it off”. With a three-word verb, however, the pronoun goes at the end: “look forward to it”.
text.es: El pronombre no puede ir después del adverbio: no «turn off it», sino «turn it off». Con un verbo de tres palabras, en cambio, el pronombre va al final: «look forward to it».

text.en: Learn a phrasal verb together with its meaning, not word for word: “give up” is not “give upward”, and “put off” is not “put away”. In Spanish it often matches one verb: posponer, rendirse.
text.es: Aprende un phrasal verb junto con su significado, no palabra por palabra: «give up» no es «dar arriba», y «put off» no es «poner fuera». En español suele corresponder a un solo verbo: posponer, rendirse.

speak.en: A phrasal verb is a verb plus an adverb or preposition whose meaning is not the sum of the words: «give up» means stop trying, «put off» means postpone. With a separable phrasal verb the pronoun goes between the two parts: «turn it off», not «turn off it». With an inseparable one the object follows the whole verb: «look after them». Three-word verbs are for example «run out of» and «look forward to». After «look forward to» comes the -ing form.
speak.es: Un phrasal verb es un verbo más un adverbio o preposición cuyo significado no es la suma de las palabras: «give up» significa rendirse, «put off» significa posponer. Con un phrasal verb separable el pronombre va entre las dos partes: «turn it off», no «turn off it». Con uno no separable el objeto va después de todo el verbo: «look after them». Verbos de tres palabras son por ejemplo «run out of» y «look forward to». Después de «look forward to» va la forma -ing.

why.en: Give up means to stop trying.
why.es: Give up significa dejar de intentar.

make.en: Make up has a different meaning (invent, reconcile); “keep trying” asks for give up.
make.es: Make up tiene otro significado (inventar, reconciliarse); «keep trying» pide give up.

take.en: Take up has a different meaning (start a hobby); “keep trying” asks for give up.
take.es: Take up tiene otro significado (empezar un pasatiempo); «keep trying» pide give up.

tr.en: Don't give up! Keep trying.

items.sentence: We had to ___ off the meeting until Monday.

take.en: “Take off the meeting” does not express postponing; put off does.
take.es: «Take off the meeting» no expresa posponer; put off sí.

get.en: “Get off the meeting” does not express postponing; put off does.
get.es: «Get off the meeting» no expresa posponer; put off sí.

tr.en: We had to put off the meeting until Monday.
tr.es: Tuvimos que posponer la junta hasta el lunes.

items.sentence: She ___ up with a great idea.

why.en: Come up with means to think of.
why.es: Come up with significa ocurrírsele a alguien.

went.en: “Go up with” does not mean thinking of; come up with does.
went.es: «Go up with» no significa ocurrirse; come up with sí.

got.en: “Get up with” is not a phrasal verb in this meaning; you need come up with.
got.es: «Get up with» no es un phrasal verb en este sentido; hace falta come up with.

examples: He came up with a plan.
Can you come up with one?

tr.en: She came up with a great idea.
tr.es: A ella se le ocurrió una gran idea.

why.en: Run out of means to have none left.
why.es: Run out of significa quedarse sin.

up.en: “Run up of” does not exist in this meaning; you need run out of.
up.es: «Run up of» no existe en este sentido; hace falta run out of.

off.en: “Run off of” does not express running low; you need run out of.
off.es: «Run off of» no expresa quedarse sin; hace falta run out of.

tr.en: We have run out of milk.

on.en: Turn on means to switch on; refusing an offer needs turn down.
on.es: Turn on significa encender; rechazar una oferta necesita turn down.

at.en: “Turn at” does not exist in this meaning; you need turn down.
at.es: «Turn at» no existe en este sentido; hace falta turn down.

tr.en: He turned down the job offer.
tr.es: Él rechazó la oferta de trabajo.

items.sentence: They ___ off the game because of the rain.

looked.en: “Look off the game” does not express cancelling; you need call off.
looked.es: «Look off the game» no expresa cancelar; hace falta call off.

turned.en: “Turn off the game” does not express cancelling; you need call off.
turned.es: «Turn off the game» no expresa cancelar; hace falta call off.

tr.en: They called off the game because of the rain.
tr.es: Cancelaron el juego por la lluvia.

why.en: Turn off means to switch off; the object can go between the two parts.
why.es: Turn off significa apagar; el objeto puede ir entre las dos partes.

of.en: Of is a preposition, not the particle of the phrasal verb; you need off.
of.es: Of es una preposición, no la partícula del phrasal verb; hace falta off.

to.en: “Turn the light to” does not mean switching off; you need off.
to.es: «Turn the light to» no significa apagar; hace falta off.

tr.en: Please turn the light off.

items.sentence: The lights are on. Please turn ___ off.

why.en: The pronoun goes between the two parts, in the object form: turn them off.
why.es: El pronombre va entre las dos partes, en forma de objeto: turn them off.

they.en: They is the subject form; between turn … off you need the object form (them).
they.es: They es la forma de sujeto; entre turn … off hace falta la forma de objeto (them).

their.en: Their is a possessive; here you need a personal pronoun (them).
their.es: Their es un posesivo; aquí hace falta un pronombre personal (them).

tr.en: The lights are on. Please turn them off.
tr.es: Las luces están prendidas. Por favor, apágalas.

items.sentence: She looks ___ her little brother while their parents work.

why.en: Look after means to take care of.
why.es: Look after significa cuidar a alguien.

at.en: Look at means to watch, not to take care of.
at.es: Look at significa mirar, no cuidar.

over.en: Look over means to check through, not to take care of.
over.es: Look over significa revisar, no cuidar.

tr.en: She looks after her little brother while their parents work.
tr.es: Ella cuida a su hermanito mientras sus papás trabajan.

why.en: After look forward comes to, followed by the -ing form.
why.es: Después de look forward va to, seguido de la forma -ing.

for.en: “Look forward for” does not exist; you need look forward to.
for.es: «Look forward for» no existe; hace falta look forward to.

at.en: “Look forward at” does not exist; you need look forward to.
at.es: «Look forward at» no existe; hace falta look forward to.

examples: She looks forward to meeting you.

tr.en: I'm looking forward to seeing you.

items.sentence: I can't put up ___ the noise any longer.

why.en: Put up with means to tolerate.

to.en: “Put up to” does not mean tolerate; you need put up with.
to.es: «Put up to» no significa aguantar; hace falta put up with.

for.en: “Put up for” does not mean tolerate; you need put up with.
for.es: «Put up for» no significa aguantar; hace falta put up with.

tr.en: I can't put up with the noise any longer.
tr.es: Ya no puedo aguantar el ruido.

why.en: Get over means to recover from.

up.en: Get up means to rise; recovering from an illness needs get over.
up.es: Get up significa levantarse; recuperarse de una enfermedad necesita get over.

out.en: Get out means to leave; recovering needs get over.
out.es: Get out significa salir; recuperarse necesita get over.

examples: It took time to get over it.

tr.en: He finally got over his cold.
tr.es: Él finalmente se recuperó de su resfriado.

items.sentence: My car broke ___ on the way to work.

why.en: Break down means to stop working.

off.en: Break off means to snap or stop, not to stop working.
off.es: Break off significa romperse o interrumpirse, no descomponerse.

over.en: “Break over” does not exist in this meaning; you need break down.
over.es: «Break over» no existe en este sentido; hace falta break down.

tr.en: My car broke down on the way to work.
tr.es: Mi carro se descompuso camino al trabajo.

why.en: Fill out means to complete a form (the usual American form).
why.es: Fill out significa llenar un formulario (la forma habitual en inglés americano).

on.en: “Fill on” does not exist in this meaning; you need fill out.
on.es: «Fill on» no existe en este sentido; hace falta fill out.

at.en: “Fill at” does not exist in this meaning; you need fill out.
at.es: «Fill at» no existe en este sentido; hace falta fill out.

tr.en: Please fill out this form.

items.sentence: We ran ___ an old friend at the airport.

why.en: Run into means to meet by chance.
why.es: Run into significa encontrarse por casualidad.

up.en: “Run up” someone does not mean meeting; you need run into.
up.es: «Run up» a alguien no significa encontrarse; hace falta run into.

off.en: Run off means to run away, not to meet.
off.es: Run off significa salir corriendo, no encontrarse.

tr.en: We ran into an old friend at the airport.
tr.es: Nos encontramos a un viejo amigo en el aeropuerto.

items.sentence: She grew ___ in a small town.

why.en: Grow up means to become an adult.

down.en: “Grow down” does not exist; you need grow up.
down.es: «Grow down» no existe; hace falta grow up.

off.en: “Grow off” does not exist in this meaning; you need grow up.
off.es: «Grow off» no existe en este sentido; hace falta grow up.

tr.en: She grew up in a small town.
tr.es: Ella creció en un pueblo pequeño.

items.sentence: I need to carry ___ with my work.

in.en: “Carry in with” does not exist; you need carry on.
in.es: «Carry in with» no existe; hace falta carry on.

at.en: “Carry at with” does not exist; you need carry on.
at.es: «Carry at with» no existe; hace falta carry on.

tr.en: I need to carry on with my work.
Don't give up.
